youtube_title: The LaPorte congressman who went to expose a seance (and came back a believer)
body: Charles Cathcart farmed near LaPorte, served in Congress (1845-1849) and briefly in the U.S. Senate (1852-1853). A skeptic, he went to a spirit circle at the Poston home in LaPorte County to expose it, armed with a homemade device that could light the dark room in a flash. When the lights went out, a 'spirit' the circle called Old King began to beat a bass drum. Cathcart hit his light, and wrote in the Spiritual Telegraph that the stick beat the drum 'as if handled from above, and no mortal nearer than about eight feet of it!' The skeptic became a believer and started a spirit circle of his own. 🥁 Comment your town, and it could be next! #LaPorte #LaPorteCounty #Indiana #History #Seance #LaPorteAfterDark
credit: All pictures are drawn (illustrations). Narration is a computer voice. Sources: Indiana Historical Bureau, Talking Hoosier History, 'Spiritualism: Beyond the Spectacle' (2019), quoting Cathcart's account in the Spiritual Telegraph; Biographical Directory of the U.S. Congress and Wikipedia (Charles W. Cathcart); Emma Hardinge, Modern American Spiritualism (1870), ch. 32, 'Cathcart's spirit room'; Indiana Historical Society; Transatlantica.
